2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:8493

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani
 On The 30th Of January, 2026
 Criminal Appeal No. 11639 of 2025
 Anil Tekam
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Nitesh Kumr Jain - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Himanshu Soni - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State
 Order

The appellant has filed this third criminal appeal under Section 14-A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 being aggrieved by order dated 24.09.2025 passed in SCATR No.121/2018 passed by the Special Judge under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Balaghat, MP whereby his bail application filed under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023, has been rejected.

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the present appellant that the present appellant is in custody since 02.10.2024.
This is third bail application.
Earlier two bail applications have been dismissed as withdrawn.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:8493 2 CRA-11639-2025
It is also submitted that as many as four witnesses have been examined including the parents of the victim.
Though they have supported the story but they are not the eye witnesses to the incident.
They have been narrated the story by the prosecutrix but prosecutrix herself is absconded and could not be traced by the prosecution despite the order of this Court dated 16.12.2025.
Since the prosecutix is absconded for long time, the present appellant may be released on bail.
He has no criminal antecedents.
He is ready to comply with the stringent conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
Therefore, it is prayed that the appellant may be granted benefit of bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application/appeal and prayed for its rejection.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6 . Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and the entire facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is inclined to release the present appellant on bail.

Thus, without commenting on the merits of the case, the appeal is allowed and it is directed that appellant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.70,000/- (Rupees Seventy Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court/Committal Court.
8 . Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance by the office of this Court.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE DV Anil Tekam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86589243/
